expectation_provenance_labels.static-derived; not observed reference o: derived from evidence reviewed before sanitization
expectation_provenance_labels.extracted execution (x86_64 slice, glibc: the original program's x86_64 code that computes the value ran on the case's inputs, on a Linux x86_64 host with glibc in place of the macOS system libraries (base-10 exponential and cosine); nothing that supplies these inputs from a document, a control or the audio path ran, and nothing that applies the results to audio

stated_assumptions: Static-derived (carried): a mixer number written as plain decimal text is read as the nearest binary32 number; a code's name is its list entry; some display shows the value texts, computed from the value as read; the base-10 logarithm may differ in the last binary32 digit, so inputs near a text boundary have no expectation.

The macOS arm64 build computes these values as the x86_64 build does, within each case's comparison. Its fused multiply-adds can change the last binary32 digit of the Dipped and Intermediate levels, of the pan-law gains (through binary64 intermediate results only) and of the three curve points next to the bottom of each fader curve; the comparisons cover these, and MIXER-VALUES-051, which uses one of those points, moves by less than 1e-8 for a one-step change. All extracted-execution cases depend on it.
The reference's base-10 exponential and cosine are within one binary32 step of glibc's at these inputs; the comparisons allow one step.

The round-trip cases (MIXER-VALUES-058 to 064) compare exactly. They assume that the reference's base-10 exponential gives each of the curve points involved as the binary32 value nearest to the exact result, as the glibc run did; each exact result lies at least 0.16 of a binary32 step from a rounding midpoint, so an exponential that errs by less than 0.66 of a step gives the same points.
